12. Culture and civilisation

Built, with gaps Culture Module – Specification; Culture Module – Lore Specification.

The core of version 1 stands: ways of life, 144 technologies (was 138), deposits, competence and corruption, the strains of decline, fortification, states, rulers and ruled, rivers as frontiers, the focus state. New, all built:

AreaWhat it does
Calamitiesa wandering climate anomaly; failed harvests and famine; plague that spreads by land and sea; eruptions, earthquakes, floods and storms by the ground; each wears down the states it strikes
The present ruleuntil: { techs } stops the history when a people knows them all. The Creation stops at iron, writing and the castle (at most 20 000 years)
Religiondomains weighted by way of life, land, sky, learning and what befell the people; forms from animism to monotheism and philosophy; organisation; described gods; cosmology, afterlife, rites; a role for each moon; calendars; state cults; faiths descend, reform, blend and convert with the cultures
Magicoff by default (none, low, medium, high); a source, cost, limit, schools, hot spots; gifted shares by species (mana_sensitive ×4); each culture’s tradition and attitude
Myth and mythic historyeach culture’s myths, saying what they rest on; BWM’s five eras (Cosmic, Ordering, Ancient Civilisation, Cataclysm, Age of Peoples) as told (cultural frame) or as the setting’s own history (divine frame)
The lost civilisationemergent (fallen states, with ruins by the durability of their material, lost technology, a cataclysm) or ancient (an invented precursor people and cataclysm), or both
Titles and lawgovernment styles (including clan-hold for dwarves, court for elves, warband for orcs), titles written into the realms, succession, law, justice, property, bondage, taxes
Cities and routestowns, cities, great cities, metropolises with roles; routes between the 160 biggest cities with flow, goods and chokepoints
Warseach run of conquests as a war with battles, sieges, fronts, outcome and cause; the changing map over time
The present agethe largest states with government, faith, learning, wars, rivals and trade; the learning of the world by field; the open struggles; the state of magic

Still to build Magic acting on the history, trade through time, names for the lore

  • Magic is a tradition and a set of places. It does not yet change population, war or technology.
  • Trade routes are built from the end state. Goods and prices do not move through time.
  • Calamities leave no ruins unless they destroyed the seat of a fallen state.
  • Gods, titles, ruins and peoples are described and numbered, not yet named.
